clue.text: Southern county hotel has internet provider, free

parts.note: Bucks is the short name of Buckinghamshire, a county in southern England
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
EE is a British telecoms and broadband company

explanation.surface: A hotel in the Home Counties throws in its broadband at no charge.
explanation.walkthrough: BUCKSHEE is British slang, from army use in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckshee is informal British slang for something given without charge, gratis.

clue.text: Sailor after degree in rock?

indicators.note: after puts the sailor word following the degree

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
an old salt is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor with a degree, perhaps, is studying geology.
explanation.definitionFit: Basalt is a dark volcanic rock, the commonest kind formed from lava.

clue.text: Inferior crown seen on headless Egyptian's body?

indicators.note: seen on, in a down clue, puts the crown letters above the next piece

parts.note: CR is an abbreviation for crown

indicators.note: headless removes the first letter of the Egyptian body word

parts.note: an embalmed body from ancient Egypt is a mummy

explanation.surface: A shoddy crown sits on a decapitated Egyptian mummy.
explanation.definitionFit: Crummy is informal for shoddy or of poor quality.

clue.text: Block counter in market

definitions.meaning: a trader's stand at a market

explanation.surface: A trader's stand gets in the way at the market.
explanation.definitionFit: Stall means to obstruct progress and also a stand from which goods are sold.

clue.text: Digitally combined, you might say — as it's transpired

definitions.note: ... in the sense of became known or turned out

parts.note: e- stands for electronic, the prefix of digital things such as e-mail
merged means combined

explanation.surface: Files combined on a computer, as it turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you might say' flags that E for 'digitally' is a loose, informal equation.
explanation.definitionFit: When something has emerged it has come to light, just as it has transpired.

clue.text: Boatman with Indian food, it's said

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so the word for the food is heard rather than written

parts.note: a bhaji is a fried Indian vegetable fritter, often onion

explanation.surface: A man on a boat is linked with a curry-house snack.
explanation.walkthrough: BHAJI said in a British accent comes out like BARGEE; a bargee works a canal barge.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargee is the person who crews or skippers a barge on a canal or river.

clue.text: Damaged items Dora eventually wrote off

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dora finally wrote off some broken goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eventually' belongs to the definition: amortising writes a cost off gradually.
explanation.definitionFit: To amortise is to reduce a debt or asset value bit by bit over time.

clue.text: Drug found in quantities in these vessels

indicators.note: found in places the drug letter inside the quantities word

parts.note: gallons are quantities of liquid
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Drugs are smuggled in bulk aboard old ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Galleons were large sailing ships used from the 15th to 18th centuries.

clue.text: Do fish, later on in the day

parts.note: a do is a party or event
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A suggestion to go fishing in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a verb but is a noun for a social function.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is an old word for evening, the latter part of the day.

clue.text: South American university wise guys making bangers!

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
sages are wise men

explanation.surface: Clever scholars from an American campus produce something explosive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bangers' suggests fireworks, but it is British slang for sausages.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangers is everyday British slang for sausages, as in bangers and mash.

clue.text: Attempt a whopper, for one who tries to stop all attempts?

definitions.text: one who tries to stop all attempts?

parts.note: to have a go is to make an attempt
a whopper is a big lie

explanation.surface: Someone tries telling a huge fib to a person who blocks every effort.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'attempts' a goalie stops are shots at goal, a playful second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A goalkeeper's job is to stop every shot the opposition tries to score with.

clue.text: Lowlife types coming up for A-lister

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: rats are contemptible people

explanation.surface: Low characters climb the ladder to become celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a celebrity of the top rank, an A-lister.

clue.text: In artificial illumination, cut end off meat and pickle

indicators.note: cutting the end off the meat word drops its final letter

parts.note: lamb is a kind of meat
to be in a pickle is to be in a plight, a predicament

explanation.surface: Under electric light, someone trims meat and preserves it in vinegar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickle' looks like food to go with the meat, but it means a fix: PLIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamplight is the glow given off by a lamp, an artificial rather than natural light.

clue.text: Article given short measure, amounting to stealing

parts.note: the is the definite article
ft is the short form of foot, a unit of measure

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper giving short weight is little better than a thief.
explanation.definitionFit: Theft is the act of stealing property belonging to someone else.

clue.text: Copper left in compartment

indicators.note: in says the left letter is placed within the compartment word

parts.note: a pod is a detachable compartment, as on a craft

explanation.surface: A police officer has been left behind in a cell or pod.
explanation.walkthrough: PLOD is British slang for a police officer, from Mr Plod in the Noddy books.
explanation.definitionFit: Plod is British slang for an ordinary police officer, as copper is.

clue.text: Cuts in prices of delicate fabrics

indicators.note: of reverses the clue's order, so the fabric word is written before the prices word

parts.note: lace is a delicate openwork fabric
rates are prices or charges

explanation.surface: A retailer slashes the price of fine lace.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacerates means tears or gashes the flesh, a word for cuts.

clue.text: Bow: ready to begin performance?

parts.note: a violinist rubs resin on the bow hair before playing; the clue reads like a bow from the stage

explanation.surface: A performer takes a bow before the show has even started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' suggests a stage bow; it is a violin bow, treated with rosin so it grips the strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A string player's bow is rubbed with rosin to make it grip, so a bow so treated is ready to play.

clue.text: Musical piece given in public, by river

parts.note: overt means open, done in public
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A concert is performed openly by a riverside.
explanation.definitionFit: An overture is an orchestral piece played at the start of an opera or concert.

clue.text: Well fed, in West Midlands town, with Ulstermen's party

parts.note: Stoke-on-Trent, often just Stoke, is a city in the West Midlands region of England
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Visitors from Ulster are given a hearty meal in Stoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoked up is informal for having eaten heartily, like a fire well loaded with fuel.

clue.text: Holy see tax I preserve

parts.note: VAT is value added tax
to can food is to preserve it in tins

explanation.surface: The Holy See pays a tax that I must keep.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vatican is the seat of the Pope, often called the Holy See.

clue.text: Food discovered in Bono's hideout

indicators.note: discovered in means the letters are found inside the following words

explanation.surface: Snacks are found in the singer Bono's secret retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is informal British slang for food.

clue.text: Southern county with many hotel places?

definitions.meaning: The short name of Bedfordshire, an English county north of London
a hotel offers many ..., places to sleep

explanation.surface: A county in the south has plenty of hotel rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedfordshire is shortened to Beds, and beds are the sleeping places a hotel lets out.

clue.text: Born a woodsman — now an internet sensation?

parts.note: a logger fells trees

explanation.surface: A lumberjack by birth has become famous online.
explanation.definitionFit: A blogger writes online, and a popular one can become a web celebrity; the question mark admits not all are.

clue.text: When you're out of this, you're not with it, on balance

definitions.text: When you're out of this, you're not with it, on balance

parts.words: When you're out of this, you're not with it, on balance
parts.note: out of this phrase means off-balance or awry

explanation.surface: Someone muses that losing one's balance leaves one confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of kilter means out of balance or working wrongly.

clue.text: Glues pieces of wood

definitions.meaning: ... as a verb, fixes with adhesive

explanation.surface: Someone glues together bits of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Sticks means fastens with glue and also names small branches or lengths of wood.

clue.text: Strut with back part pointing backwards, enclosing top of kingpost

indicators.note: enclosing means the reversed word goes round the next letter
pointing backwards means the back part word is read in reverse

parts.note: the rear is the back part of anything

indicators.note: top of means the first letter of kingpost, which comes first in a down-reading sense

explanation.surface: A builder describes a roof strut angled backwards around the kingpost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointing backwards' turns REAR into RAER; 'enclosing' puts the K (top of kingpost) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A raker is a sloping strut or prop, such as one shoring up a wall.

clue.text: Final selection of those from whom seven are chosen to appear with Snow White?

definitions.meaning: the final group of candidates chosen from

definitions.text: those from whom seven are chosen to appear with Snow White?
definitions.meaning: read as a list of short people from which the seven dwarfs are cast

explanation.surface: A casting director narrows candidates down for the Seven Dwarfs in a pantomime.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortlist is the select group from which a winner is chosen; whimsically, it lists short people.

clue.text: Also time to get husband a canine, perhaps

parts.note: too means also

explanation.surface: It is time for the husband to get a dog as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canine' suggests a dog, but here it is a pointed tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A canine is one of the pointed teeth, so it is an example of a tooth.

clue.text: Latest report: at university, with boyfriend?

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge
a date is someone you go out with

explanation.surface: News from a student: settled in at college and seeing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An update is the most recent piece of news or information on something.

clue.text: One who doesn't entirely believe in initially culling goats, confounded

indicators.note: confounded means mixed up, so the letters are thrown into a new order
initially means the first letter of culling

explanation.surface: A sceptic is unconvinced about a cull of goats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confounded' scrambles IN plus GOATS to AGNOSTI; 'initially' supplies the C of culling at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnostic holds that God's existence cannot be known, so neither believes fully nor denies.

clue.text: Article revealing scandal with former model

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
to model is to pose for an artist or photographer

explanation.surface: A tabloid story uncovers a scandal involving a one-time model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a part of speech, but it is a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposé is a piece of journalism that uncovers wrongdoing or scandal.

clue.text: Places to grow fruit, or varieties of beetroot?

parts.note: chard is a leaf beet, the same species as beetroot, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A gardener weighs fruit trees against different kinds of beet.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plot planted with fruit trees.
